1.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 1

Week 1 is done. A few of you looked ready for football. A few of you looked like you drafted on a toilet and forgot to flush.

Matt scored the most. Erik scored the least. Tony and Sam each had a win on the bench. Jake got his rivalry lead beaten out of him. Week 2 is here—set a lineup that doesn't make me want to file a welfare check.

Brian Corrigan|Erik Mannarino.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: ASHTON PLENTY, ERIK EMPTY
Brian Corrigan|Erik Mannarino.body:
Brian 130.40, Erik 101.86 | Brian leads 11–7

No hangover for the defending champ. Jeanty put up 33, Amon-Ra 28, and the Jaguars defense 15 after getting to play against what looked like a JV offense. Brian had a few guys do absolutely nothing, and it didn't matter.

Erik reached for the Rams defense early just to watch it give him negative points. Taylor gave him 25. McBride gave him 24. The rest of the team acted like they'd just gotten off a flight from Australia and were too fucking tired to play.

Deebo scored 18 on Erik's bench while Quentin Johnston scored 3 in his flex. That was stupid, but don't start with the “if I played Deebo” bullshit. Brian won by almost 29. Erik had the lowest score in the league and got his ass kicked on the biggest stage of the week.

Paul Deutsch|Shawn Smutak.title: ZAY POWERS, SMUTAK'S LIGHTS OUT
Paul Deutsch|Shawn Smutak.body:
Paul 154.80, Shawn 132.81 | Paul adds to his historical H2H lead

Dart scored 26. Zay scored 29 before his hamstring gave out. Pittsburgh's defense scored 20. Ja'Marr Chase scored 3, and Paul still had the second-highest total in the league. That's a fucking annoying team to lose to.

Jefferson put up 31 and Olave 28 for Shawn. Four other starters couldn't even get to double digits. Hampton gave him 8, Dobbins 3, and Jameson 8. JJ and Olave were trying to keep the boat afloat while the rest of those assholes took turns punching holes in it.

Paul beat Shawn last year, too. Apparently Deutsch ruining my Sunday is now league history.

Steve Cegelka|Tony Yokiel.title: BOSTON ON THE BENCH, TONY IN THE LOSS COLUMN
Steve Cegelka|Tony Yokiel.body:
Steve 118.11, Tony 111.12 | Steve adds another H2H win

“The Bye Week” came back and immediately scored the third-lowest total in the league. Puka scored 12. DeVonta 8. Adams 5. Kittle 3. Houston's defense went negative. Fucking inspiring stuff, Tony.

Steve had his own collection of useless starts—Waddle 1, Terry 3, Pollard 4—but Henry ran for 36, JSN scored 27, and Bucky added 20. His best guys showed up. That's all it took. Steve is a one-time champion; Tony has three titles and somehow still couldn't find the winning flex play on his own bench.

Tony was buried heading into Monday, and Kenneth Walker came out blazing for 39. It nearly worked. You know what would have worked? Starting Denzel Boston's 14 instead of Adams's 5. With the actual unrounded points, Tony wins by 2.31 on that swap. The winning lineup was sitting on his bench while the three-time champ watched his season start 0–1.

Matt Rennert|Michael Clark.title: GIBBS ME THAT
Matt Rennert|Michael Clark.body:
Matt 156.79, Mike 121.56 | Matt leads their owner-era series 1–0

I picked Matt to win the championship. He responded with the highest score in Week 1, because now he's going to be even more unbearable. Gibbs scored 34, Monty 28, and Javonte 24. Gibbs and Montgomery aren't even teammates anymore and they're still finding ways to fuck up someone else's Sunday.

Mike got 37 out of Josh Allen and still lost by 35. CMC gave him 13. Denver's defense went negative. Kincaid scored 18 on the bench while Fannin scored 4, but that wasn't going to save Mike either.

And no, we're not counting some old franchise's games to pretend these two had a rivalry. Matt and Mike were 0–0 as owners before this. Matt's first entry in their H2H book is a beating.

Jake Stacy|John DeBrouse.title: CHRISTIAN GIGAWATSON, JAKE IN THE SHITTER
Jake Stacy|John DeBrouse.body:
John 146.87, Jake 106.46 | H2H tied 6–6

Jake came in leading this rivalry 6–5. John tied it up by beating him by more than 40 fucking points.

Swift put up 33, Likely 27, and Watson 35. John even had Jalen Coker's 36 sitting on his bench. Jake should thank him for that much mercy.

Lamar scored 28 for Jake. After that? A.J. Brown 5, Rashee Rice 9, LaPorta 9, and Wan'Dale 8. Five single-digit starters overall. Jake was the second-lowest scoring team in the league and managed to turn a close historical rivalry into a Week 1 public execution.

Reid Masters|Sam Young.title: GHOST IN LOVELAND, MONANGAI IN THE WRONG PLACE
Reid Masters|Sam Young.body:
Reid 138.55, Sam 128.06 | Reid leads 4–0

Reid did what Reid always does. Lawrence scored 25, Bijan 31, DJ Moore 22, and the team had enough everywhere else to absorb Pickens's 5 and Dowdle's 4. Four meetings with Sam. Four wins.

Sam got 36 from Caleb while the Bears scored 59 points, and Loveland still managed zero catches and zero fantasy points. I'll give Sam that one—that's some cursed bullshit.

Congrats, Sam: you're the first CPBFFL owner to break 25,000 career points. You're at 25,049.70. That's a huge fucking milestone, even if this week's RB2 choice turned the celebration into another loss.

But Blake Corum's 5 over Kyle Monangai's 25? That's on you. Use the real, unrounded points and that one switch gives Sam a 148.06–138.55 win. Instead, Reid beats him again because Sam left the answer sitting on the fucking bench.

2.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 2

WEEK 2 REVIEW

Well, we officially confirmed that nobody does their homework, nobody reads before voting, and apparently nobody—including me—bothered to properly review the defensive scoring system.

The good news is that we fixed it. Good defensive performances will now actually be rewarded instead of a defense getting treated like shit regardless of how well it played. We also went back and checked every matchup from the first two weeks. Luckily, the scoring correction did not change a single winner.

So nobody gets to use that as an excuse.

Steve scored the most. Reid scored the least. Mike dropped 162 points and somehow walked away 0–2. Sam produced the lowest winning score of the week, while John delivered the biggest ass-kicking.

We also had three close games that could have been flipped by one correct lineup decision. Those owners will not be receiving sympathy. They will have their mistake blasted directly into their fucking face.

Shawn Smutak|Brian Corrigan.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: OLAVE THIS WIN, NABERS CAN’T SAVE YOU
Shawn Smutak|Brian Corrigan.body:
Shawn Smutak 113.04 – Brian Corrigan 106.51

Shawn leads the H2H series 10–7 | Both teams are 1–1

The projected scenario played out almost perfectly. Shawn carried a small lead into Monday night, and Malik Nabers needed only seven points to steal the Game of the Week for Brian.

Then Nabers dislocated his shoulder, Jameis Winston started throwing passes at his feet, and Brian’s Monday-night comeback died almost immediately. Nabers finished with 1 point, Jacksonville’s defense went negative, and three other starters failed to reach six.

Brian still got 35 from Amon-Ra and 29 from Dak. Two guys tried dragging the rest of this lineup across the finish line while Nabers’s shoulder and Winston’s accuracy told them to go fuck themselves.

Shawn wasn’t exactly dominant. Jefferson scored 8, Jameson 5 and Dobbins 3. But Olave scored 22, Diggs added 21, Hampton gave him 17 and Tyler Warren put up 14. It wasn’t pretty, but Shawn had fewer useless assholes in his starting lineup.

Now for the decision that should haunt Brian: Jake Ferguson scored 20 on the bench while old man Mark Andrews scored 10. That single decision cost Brian 9.4 points. Make the correct call and Brian wins 115.91–113.04.

Andrews over Ferguson single-handedly lost Brian the Game of the Week.

Sucks to suck.

Reid Masters|John DeBrouse.title: CEEDEE YA LATER, INJURYAPOLIS FLATLINES
Reid Masters|John DeBrouse.body:
John DeBrouse 114.07 – Reid Masters 72.95

Historical H2H tied 3–3 | John moves to 2–0; Reid falls to 1–1

Reid’s week started going to hell Thursday night when DJ Moore left early and finished with negative points. Then Dallas Goedert went down Sunday after scoring 1. By that point, Injuryapolis was living up to its fucking name and the roster never recovered.

Reid finished with the lowest score in the league. Jeremiyah Love scored 7, Matthew Golden scored 9, Cam Skattebo scored 9 and the entire starting lineup produced only four double-digit performances.

The bench makes it look even worse. Jonah Coleman scored 14, Josh Downs scored 14 and Juwan Johnson scored 10. Starting those three over Love, Moore and Goedert adds more than 30 points—and Reid still loses. That’s how thoroughly John beat his ass.

CeeDee Lamb carried John with 35 points. Jalen Coker and Christian Watson added 14 each, while Swift chipped in 12. Drake Maye scored only 7, but John could have started a traffic cone at quarterback and still won comfortably.

John delivered the biggest blowout of Week 2, beating Reid by 41.12 points and moving to 2–0.

Injuryapolis didn’t just lose. It fucking flatlined.

Paul Deutsch|Erik Mannarino.title: DART MISFIRES, CRUISERS FINALLY LEAVE PORT
Paul Deutsch|Erik Mannarino.body:
Erik Mannarino 106.63 – Paul Deutsch 79.60

Erik leads the H2H series 8–5 | Both teams are 1–1

Yep, this is usually the week when Paul starts wondering whether he wants to return next season.

Every year, some major injury or ridiculous disaster seems to find him. This one probably hurts even worse after Jaxson Dart looked so good last week, only to go down on the first drive and finish with less than one point.

Paul climbed to No. 2 in the power rankings and immediately scored the second-lowest total of the week. Jayden Reed scored 1. Tucker Kraft, Jakobi Meyers and Rhamondre Stevenson each scored 3. Ja’Marr Chase put up 26 and basically spent Sunday screaming for someone—anyone—to help him.

But the injury isn’t what should really piss Paul off.

Paul spent the week debating between Dart and Brock Purdy. He chose Dart. Purdy scored 28 on the bench while Dart scored 0.

That decision cost Paul 27.68 points. Make the correct choice and Paul wins 107.28–106.63 by less than one point.

Paul didn’t lose because his roster was hopeless. Paul stared directly at the winning decision, picked the other quarterback, and watched his week die on the first drive.

Erik didn’t need greatness. Jonathan Taylor scored 29, McBride and the Rams defense each scored 18, and everybody else simply avoided becoming Jaxson Dart.

After being the Week 1 punching bag, the Cruisers finally leave port. Erik gets the win and extends his historical lead over Paul to 8–5.

Matt Rennert|Tony Yokiel.title: DAVANTE’S INFERNO BURNS THE PRESEASON CHAMP
Matt Rennert|Tony Yokiel.body:
Tony Yokiel 153.16 – Matt Rennert 121.48

Historical H2H tied 1–1 | Both teams are 1–1

This looked like an easy Matt victory after Thursday night.

Goff scored 29, Gibbs added 23 and Matt appeared ready to prove that his Week 1 performance wasn’t a fluke. Tony’s lineup looked like it was heading toward another loss, especially when Puka Nacua was ruled out just before game time.

Then Monday night arrived and Davante Adams told Matt to go fuck himself.

Adams exploded for 39. DeVonta Smith scored 27, Kenneth Walker added 24 and George Kittle put up 18. Tony went from the third-lowest scorer in Week 1 to the second-highest scorer in Week 2 and beat the preseason championship favorite by more than 31.

Tony even left Tre Tucker’s 23 and Denzel Boston’s 23 on the bench because apparently scoring 153 wasn’t obnoxious enough.

Matt got 16 from Garrett Wilson and 13 from Seattle’s defense, but Montgomery scored 4 and Michael Mayer scored 5 while Rashod Bateman’s 21 sat on the bench. Bateman wouldn’t have saved him, but it would have made the final score slightly less embarrassing.

Matt remains dangerous, but his Week 1 coronation lasted exactly seven days before Tony shoved the imaginary crown directly up his ass.

Steve Cegelka|Michael Clark.title: JSN AND THE 176-POINT FUCK-YOU
Steve Cegelka|Michael Clark.body:
Steve Cegelka 176.18 – Michael Clark 162.37

Steve leads the H2H series 3–2 | Steve moves to 2–0; Mike falls to 0–2

Speaking of regretting joining the league, Mike has to be feeling that right about now.

Mike scored 162—the third-highest total of the entire week—and still lost by almost 14. Josh Allen scored 41, CMC and Kincaid each scored 22, and six starters reached double digits. There was no bad lineup decision to blame. Mike got nearly everything possible from his roster and still got punched in the mouth.

Mike is now 0–2 despite scoring 281.93 points, the second-most in the league. He has also allowed a league-high 327.97 points.

That isn’t bad management. That’s the fantasy gods breaking into his house, eating everything in the refrigerator and taking a shit on the carpet before leaving.

Steve dropped a league-best 176 despite getting only 7 from Justin Herbert. JSN went nuclear for 45, New England’s defense scored 27, Kelce added 25, Waddle scored 21 and Henry gave him 17.

JSN now has five touchdowns through two weeks. If Kelce is actually back to his old form, this roster could become a legitimate problem for the entire league. When your quarterback shits the bed and you still outscore everyone, your team is doing something right.

Steve moves to 2–0, takes the historical series lead over Mike and reminds everyone that the one-time champion might not be fucking around this year.

Sam Young|Jake Stacy.title: SAM BARELY COOKS, JAKE STILL STARVES
Sam Young|Jake Stacy.body:
Sam Young 85.17 – Jake Stacy 81.30

Sam leads the H2H series 14–4 | Sam moves to 1–1; Jake falls to 0–2

What the shit was this?

Steve almost outscored these two teams by himself. Steve scored 176.18. Sam and Jake combined for 166.47.

This wasn’t a fantasy matchup. It was two drunks fighting over the last slice of pizza in a parking lot.

James Cook scored 21 and Parker Washington added 16 for Sam. After that, the lineup became a collection of single-digit disappointments. Caleb scored 6, Loveland scored 1 and Baltimore’s defense managed 4.

Sam didn’t cook shit. He microwaved leftovers and survived.

Jake got 17 from LaPorta, 14 from Lamar and 12 each from Achane and Rice. Wan’Dale scored 1, Addison scored 4 and Croskey-Merritt scored 5.

But Jake absolutely had a winning lineup available.

Malik Washington scored 8 on the bench while Wan’Dale Robinson scored 1. That one switch adds 6.8 points and gives Jake an 88.10–85.17 victory.

Sam gets the lowest-scoring victory of the season and extends his ridiculous historical advantage over Jake to 14–4. Jake is dead last in the standings, and the McGibblets already look like expired meat.

3.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 3

WEEK 3 REVIEW
Reid went from last week’s league-low 72 to this week’s league-high 161. Brian finished dead last with 80. John is the only team left at 3–0, while Mike and Jake are both 0–3.
For anyone wondering how bad 0–3 is in this league: from 2012–2025, only one of 23 CPBFFL teams that started 0–3 made the playoffs. Mike has scored enough to be furious about it. Jake’s roster looks like it needs its own hospital wing.
Erik escaped with the lowest-scoring win of the week. Reid delivered the biggest ass-kicking. And the Game of the Week proved that predicting Steve to beat Matt was a really fucking stupid thing for me to do.

Matt Rennert|Steve Cegelka.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: JAMIRACLE GIBBS
Matt Rennert|Steve Cegelka.body:
Matt Rennert 156.11 – Steve Cegelka 115.80

Matt leads the historical series 2–0 | Both teams are 2–1

I picked Steve to win 151–120. Matt apparently read that, told me to go fuck myself, and won by 40 instead.

Gibbs scored 41, the highest starter score in the league this week. Garrett Wilson added 26, Javonte Williams scored 18 and now Matt has Brock Bowers dropping 27 from the tight end spot. Gibbs keeps carrying his share every week, and Bowers makes a roster that was already a problem even harder to beat.

Steve got 35 from JSN and 21 from Henry. Then Herbert scored 12, Waddle 6, Schultz 6 and New England’s defense went negative. Steve scored 176 last week with little help from his quarterback. This week, the rest of the lineup didn’t bail him out.

Nix, McLaurin and Pollard all scored more than players Steve started. Put all three in and Steve still loses. Matt beat the team we’d just called a contender so thoroughly that the bench can’t even start an argument.

And I’ll admit I enjoyed one part of it: Steve has spent years seeming to face the lowest-scoring opponent in the fucking league. Welcome to what the rest of us have been dealing with. Matt takes the Game of the Week and reminds everyone why he’s No. 1.

Reid Masters|Jake Stacy.title: JUWAN JOHNSON AND THE INJURYAPOLIS RESURRECTION
Reid Masters|Jake Stacy.body:
Reid Masters 161.38 – Jake Stacy 91.74

Reid leads the historical series 7–1 | Reid moves to 2–1; Jake falls to 0–3

Last week Reid scored 72 and Injuryapolis looked ready to live up to its name. This week he scored a league-best 161 and beat Jake by 69.64—the biggest blowout of Week 3.

Bijan scored 37. Juwan Johnson added 23. Jeremiyah Love and Matthew Golden each cleared 21. Every Reid starter except the 49ers defense reached double digits. Reid is fucking back.

Jake, meanwhile, watched Achane go down. Evans went down too. The injuries keep piling up, and the healthy players aren’t doing enough to cover for them. Lamar scored 20 and Addison gave him 21, but Achane finished with 1, Croskey-Merritt scored 5 and the Eagles defense went negative.

Wan’Dale Robinson’s 18 sat on Jake’s bench. Start him and Jake still gets his ass kicked. This wasn’t a lineup mistake that decided a close game; it was a roster losing pieces while Reid ran it over.

Reid is back above .500. Jake is 0–3, last in points scored, and has lost seven of eight historical meetings with Reid. At this rate, the McGibblets need a medical staff more than a waiver claim.

Paul Deutsch|Brian Corrigan.title: GLOCK PURDY FIRES; BRIAN’S 100TH WIN MISSES
Paul Deutsch|Brian Corrigan.body:
Paul Deutsch 133.18 – Brian Corrigan 80.69

The historical series is tied 9–9 | Paul moves to 2–1; Brian falls to 1–2

Last week Paul watched Dart go down while Purdy scored 28 on his bench. This week Purdy started, scored 34, and looked like he might be the steal of the draft. Paul’s team went from a 79-point disaster right back to putting up 133.

Chase scored 24, Tuten added 17 and Flowers gave Paul 15. He even left Meyers’s 19 and Kalif Raymond’s 22 on the bench. He didn’t need either of them.

The celebration comes with a catch: Paul lost Breece Hall for the next few weeks. Apparently this team can’t have one good Sunday without the fantasy gods sending him a fucking bill.

Brian scored 80, the lowest total in the league. Jadarian Price managed 1, Nabers scored 7 and Cincinnati’s defense cost him 2. Brian has scored fewer points every week since Week 1: 132, 106, then 80. That’s not a slump; that’s a team walking backward down the stairs.

I predicted Brian would win and claim career win No. 100. Paul had other plans. He ties their historical series at 9–9 and leaves the commissioner stuck on 99.

John DeBrouse|Sam Young.title: LONDON CALLING; SAM DOESN’T ANSWER
John DeBrouse|Sam Young.body:
John DeBrouse 134.75 – Sam Young 121.86

John leads the historical series 10–7 | John moves to 3–0; Sam falls to 1–2

John might be the real deal. He’s the only undefeated team left, and now London has Tyler Shough throwing the ball more than five yards downfield. London scored 28, Shough added 23, Watson put up 22 and CeeDee gave John another 20.

Likely scored 3 and Coker scored 3, but the top of John’s lineup did enough damage to survive both of them. This roster keeps finding different ways to win.

I was too low on Sam coming into the season. Darnold scored 28, Cook gave him 20 and Burden added 19. There’s a competitive team here. But Brown scored 8, Ladd 10 and Loveland 7. His top picks keep taking turns underperforming, and against an opponent scoring 134, those missing points hurt.

Sam made it a game. John was simply better. Three weeks in, John is still perfect—and the rest of us may need to stop treating that as a cute early-season story.

Tony Yokiel|Michael Clark.title: KITTLE RED CORVETTE RUNS MIKE OVER
Tony Yokiel|Michael Clark.body:
Tony Yokiel 141.92 – Michael Clark 106.71

Tony leads the historical series 9–3 | Tony moves to 2–1; Mike falls to 0–3

Of course Mike faced The Bye Week and didn’t get a fucking bye.

Tony had five players score more than 20: Kittle, Michael Wilson, Walker, Warren and Adams. Green Bay’s defense scored negative 6, and Tony still beat Mike by 35. Apparently even Tony’s defense tried to give Mike a break and the rest of the roster refused.

It gets funnier every week—unless you’re Mike. He scored 162 and lost last week. This week his opponent threw five 20-point performances at him. Mike has scored 390.64 points, fifth-most in the league, and allowed a league-high 476.89. We know he’s boiling inside.

This time he also had a winning lineup available. Harold Fannin scored 24 on the bench while Kincaid scored 3. DK scored 12 while Shakir scored 1. Denver’s defense scored 11 while the Saints scored 1. Make those three swaps and Mike wins 147.41–141.92.

Mike has every right to hate his schedule. He also has to live with the lineup he submitted. Tony moves to 2–1; Mike moves to 0–3 and gets another week of hearing about how unlucky he is.

Erik Mannarino|Shawn Smutak.title: OMARION YAWN; THE CRUISERS SAIL PAST SHAWN
Erik Mannarino|Shawn Smutak.body:
Erik Mannarino 110.33 – Shawn Smutak 100.12

The historical series is tied 8–8 | Erik moves to 2–1; Shawn falls to 1–2

Erik scored the fewest points of any winner and still beat Shawn by 10.21, the closest finish of Week 3.

Burrow scored 22 and McBride gave him 16. Then Deebo Samuel did something ridiculous: zero receptions, but roughly 80 yards and a touchdown on one play. That one run helped win Erik the week while Shawn watched his lead disappear.

Minnesota’s defense scored 24 for Shawn. Olave added 19 and Warren scored 14. But Jefferson left early Sunday and finished with 5, putting Shawn in a horrible spot. If Jefferson misses time, a team already dealing with the loss of Jayden Daniels has a much bigger problem.

Then there’s Omarion Yawn Hampton. He scored 5, and getting out-snapped by Mitchell could be the nail in this team’s coffin if that trend continues. Hampton and Henderson combined for only 9 points from Shawn’s two starting running back spots.

Yes, Mike Washington and Chris Bell scored enough on the bench that starting both would have flipped the result. Let’s be fucking honest, though: nobody was benching Jefferson or their top picks for those guys before kickoff. That’s painful hindsight, not some obvious decision Shawn ignored.

Erik takes the narrowest win of the week and evens the historical series at 8–8. Shawn is left hoping Jefferson’s injury is brief and Hampton starts looking like the player he drafted.

4.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 4

WEEK 4 REVIEW
What a fucking week. Mike finally wins, John finally loses, Brian finally gets No. 100, and Jake is still waiting for his season to start. Meanwhile, Steve keeps collecting wins like nobody bothers checking what’s inside the fucking package.
Sunday’s injuries fucked several owners, but primetime finished the job. Reid almost chased Steve down Monday, Matt actually caught Erik, and Mike’s Sunday-night explosion left John needing a miracle. Some bench decisions could have changed things, but we’re not pretending everyone should have predicted an injury or known exactly which backup would go off.

FOUR WEEKS IN: WHO’S GETTING INTO THE PLAYOFFS?
The sixth seed always goes to the highest-scoring team outside the other five qualifiers. These historical rates include that spot and use the actual playoff teams from 2012–2025.

Four-game start — Made playoffs — Historical rate
4–0 — 10 of 11 — 90.9%
3–1 — 30 of 41 — 73.2%
2–2 — 36 of 66 — 54.5%
1–3 — 8 of 37 — 21.6%
0–4 — 0 of 13 — 0% observed

Owner — Record — Points — Historical baseline
Matt — 3–1 — 577.66 — 73.2%
Tony — 3–1 — 562.37 — 73.2%
John — 3–1 — 522.28 — 73.2%
Steve — 3–1 — 520.35 — 73.2%
Paul — 3–1 — 508.65 — 73.2%
Brian — 2–2 — 476.55 — 54.5%
Reid — 2–2 — 476.51 — 54.5%
Erik — 2–2 — 450.59 — 54.5%
Mike (current scoring wildcard) — 1–3 — 565.31 — 21.6%
Shawn — 1–3 — 464.45 — 21.6%
Sam — 1–3 — 429.91 — 21.6%

The 3–1 guys have breathing room, but 11 teams historically started there and still missed. Don’t get comfortable. Brian, Reid and Erik are sitting around a coin flip historically, while Mike’s record makes him look much worse than his actual position. He currently holds the scoring wildcard, almost 89 points ahead of Brian and Reid. The schedule can keep fucking him and he can still get in.

Sam and I share Mike’s record without sharing his scoring cushion. We need to start winning or close a significant points gap. Jake’s historical group went 0-for-13, but that isn’t elimination—he can still recover or score his way in. Being last in both categories just means he needs to get moving before the rest of us forget he’s fucking playing.

These are historical rates by record, not individual forecasts. The scoring wildcard, roster health and remaining schedule also affect each team’s outlook.

Reid Masters|Steve Cegelka.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: CAM SKAT-CRAP, STEVE SURVIVES AGAIN
Reid Masters|Steve Cegelka.body:
Steve 108.26 – Reid 103.63

H2H tied 2–2 | Steve 3–1, Reid 2–2

Sunday left Reid chasing after Love, Skattebo and Pickens combined for barely enough to buy lunch, while Moore aggravated his shoulder and finished with 2. Steve wasn’t much better—Kelce gave him 3, Bucky 6—but Bryce’s 21 on Sunday night pushed him to 108.26. Reid went into Monday needing more than 49.23 from Bijan and Johnson. Bijan gave him 32.7, Johnson added 11.9, and Steve got to watch his lead disappear until Reid stopped 4.63 short. That’s the kind of Monday where you’re afraid to get up and take a piss.

Harrison over Moore would have won it 109.13–108.26, but I’m not acting like starting Moore was some stupid fucking decision. The injury changed his afternoon. It still sucks knowing the difference was sitting on your bench. Steve gets another lowest-scoring victory and moves to 3–1 despite allowing more points than he’s scored. Apparently the schedule comes with a fucking warranty.

Shawn Smutak|Tony Yokiel.title: KEN RUNNER III RUNS SHAWN OVER
Shawn Smutak|Tony Yokiel.body:
Tony 156.67 – Shawn 118.48

Shawn leads H2H 14–10 | Tony 3–1, Shawn 1–3

Tony started Thursday with 28.5 from Warren and Boston, and I spent the rest of the weekend watching that head start become a fucking problem. Coleman gave me 23, but Puka’s 27, Kittle’s 20 and Walker’s 32 buried any chance of keeping this reasonable. By Sunday night, I needed almost 74 between Jameson and Olave. Jameson gave me 16.2, leaving Olave needing almost 58 Monday. So much for my prediction that he’d need about 14. He scored 19 and I still got my ass kicked.

No Daniels, no Jefferson, and no winning lineup hiding on the bench. Even my best combination loses comfortably. Tony has won three straight and scored 451.25 doing it. The Bye Week is handing out losses while I’m spending my Tuesdays writing about them. Fuck this.

Matt Rennert|Erik Mannarino.title: ANEMIC EGBUKA: VELE SINKS THE CRUISERS
Matt Rennert|Erik Mannarino.body:
Matt 141.28 – Erik 131.77

Matt leads H2H 2–0 | Matt 3–1, Erik 2–2

Taylor got Erik moving early Sunday, Burrow added 26, and Harvey and Deebo kept him competitive late. Barkley leaving early with a hamstring injury absolutely hurt—nobody’s benching him because they somehow know he’ll get injured. Egbuka’s 3 didn’t help either. Erik finished Sunday afternoon at 131.77 while Matt had only 73.45, but Goff, Gibbs and Waller were still coming Sunday night, with Vele waiting Monday. That 58-point cushion looked decent until Sunday night ate 47.53 of it.

Vele needed more than 10.79 Monday. He scored 17.4. Erik spent the whole weekend building a lead just to watch Matt walk him down and steal it. There was a winning bench combination, but it required several changes and replacing Barkley’s injury-shortened score. I’m not calling that obvious. Matt keeps finding enough production to cover his duds; Erik gets another week explaining how close his boat was to reaching shore before it fucking sank.

John DeBrouse|Michael Clark.title: TETAIROA McMILLIONS CASHES JOHN’S CHECK
John DeBrouse|Michael Clark.body:
Mike 174.67 – John 126.59

H2H tied 5–5 | Mike 1–3, John 3–1

Mike got a little Thursday help from Fannin, then Sunday looked like John might keep the undefeated run going when CeeDee dropped 41. Kyren and Higgins kept Mike in it, though, and after the afternoon games Mike led 111.07–96.55. John still had Shough and London Monday. Mike had McMillan and Chuba Sunday night, then the Saints’ defense. There was still a game here—until Carolina told John to go fuck himself.

McMillan and Chuba combined for 72.1, pushing Mike to 183.17 Sunday night. John’s Monday pair suddenly needed more than 86.62, depending on the Saints’ defense. New Orleans tried helping with negative 8.5, but Shough and London weren’t performing a fucking resurrection. Mike wins by 48, scores the most this week and finally gets his first win. Maye over Shough wouldn’t have saved John, either. Mike is still 1–3 with the second-most points and the most scored against him, but at least this week he got to ruin someone else’s Sunday.

Brian Corrigan|Jake Stacy.title: QUINSHON STUDKINS: BRIAN HITS 100, JAKE STILL ZERO
Brian Corrigan|Jake Stacy.body:
Brian 156.95 – Jake 92.28

Brian leads H2H 12–8 | Brian 2–2, Jake 0–4

Judkins gave Brian 21 Thursday, and Sunday never really let Jake catch his breath. WEEK 1 PREDICTIONS — RECALIBRATED

The schedule is out, team names have changed and the defense rules have been rebuilt because Sleeper cannot apply negative scoring only after 10 points or 300 yards. Under the new setup, defenses are no longer handed free points for simply existing. Points allowed are penalized continuously, yardage penalties begin at 300, and impact plays—sacks, turnovers, tackles for loss, passes defended, three-and-outs and fourth-down stops—matter more. That pulls most defenses into a tighter range and makes one touchdown or one complete defensive collapse capable of swinging a matchup.

These are SRS-style fantasy projections using the current starting lineups, the updated CPBFFL scoring, Week 1 player expectations and matchup context. Week 1 is still calibration mode, so everyone may begin preparing their excuses now.

TEAM 3 VS. YOKIEL — Pick: Tony Yokiel, 120.3–118.0. Tony finally dropped The Bye Week name, apparently hoping a rebrand would make everyone forget that he drafted Houston’s defense 100th overall. It did not. Puka projects as the biggest player in this matchup at roughly 20.5, with Hurts around 18.8. The old projection leaned Jake; the updated scoring turns this into a virtual coin flip and gives John the edge by approximately three-tenths of a point. Sam still has Cook, Chase Brown, Caleb Williams and enough young talent to make this uncomfortable—but he currently has no defense selected. Under the revised scoring, an average Week 1 defense projects around four to seven points, so filling that spot could turn this into a near toss-up. Until then, Reid owns the roster edge, the model edge and a 3-0 historical record against Sam. The former final boss is once again fighting with one hand tied behind his back, except this time he tied it himself.

Brian gets a major defensive-scoring advantage: Jacksonville projects near 7.7 while the Rams sit around 4.2. Amon-Ra also carries the highest individual expectation in the matchup at roughly 19.8. Brian leads the career series 10-7; Erik gets Week 1 by a field goal or less.

The corrected 2025 history now shows Paul winning last season, because apparently ruining my week is not a hobby for him—it is a documented tradition. Chase and Nico Collins give Paul two elite projection anchors, while Jaxson Dart only needs to avoid setting the quarterback position on fire. Shawn has Jayden Daniels, Justin Jefferson, Olave and two rookie running backs with real ceiling, but Pittsburgh’s defense carries a modest Week 1 edge over Minnesota under the new rules. The revised model cuts the old projected margin from roughly ten to about six. That is close enough for hope, which is exactly how Paul prefers to make the eventual disappointment hurt.

2026 FINAL STANDINGS & CHAMPION PREDICTION

This forecast blends roster strength, current starter projections, depth, the 14-week schedule, revised defensive scoring and a 20,000-season SRS-style simulation. Matt and Reid draw the friendliest schedules among the contenders. Steve, Tony, Brian and Sam face the roughest paths. This is not a promise; it is simply the computer volunteering to become the next league member everyone can tell to go fuck itself.

10. DOUBLE DRAKE — John DeBrouse. CeeDee, London and Maye give John a real weekly path. Roughly a 2% title chance. The model likes him more than the league does, which is the lowest possible bar.

11. TEAM 3 — Steve Cegelka. Good starters, useful depth and the hardest projected schedule in the league. Roughly a 2% title chance. If the league unexpectedly changes to three starting tight ends, move Steve directly to number one.

12. YOURDADD — Sam Young. Cook and Chase Brown are good; the roster still needs help and the schedule offers none. Less than a 1% title chance. Sam may remain the career wins leader, but the model sees the castle continuing to crumble.

CHAMPION: MATT RENNERT — VRABELS LLC. Congratulations to Matt on winning a championship that currently exists only inside a simulation. I am sure he will celebrate it with the restraint and humility for which he is famous.
